questions.q: Where does every system property actually live, regardless of whether it has a dedicated Properties page?
options: As a record in the sys_properties table
In a text configuration file deployed with each release
Inside the Business Rule that uses it
In the browser's local storage for each user
questions.explain: Every system property, whether it has a friendly UI page or not, is a row in the sys_properties table.

questions.q: A setting has no dedicated Properties page anywhere in the application navigator. How do you still reach it?
options: It cannot be changed without a developer writing a script
Navigate to the sys_properties table directly and filter by name
It must be requested from ServiceNow support
Delete and recreate the application module
questions.explain: Not every property has a dedicated page; the sys_properties table list view reaches any of them directly by name.

questions.q: What does the real property glide.sys.default_tz control?
options: The default state a new Incident opens in
Whether Service Catalog variables are required
The instance's default time zone for users without a personal time zone preference
The maximum number of scheduled jobs allowed to run concurrently
questions.explain: glide.sys.default_tz sets the instance-wide default time zone, which affects date/time display for any user without their own preference set.

questions.q: What is the real script-level API a developer uses to read a property's current value at runtime?
options: gs.getProperty('property.name')
sys_properties.read('property.name')
current.getProperty('property.name')
glide.fetchProperty('property.name')
questions.explain: gs.getProperty('name') is the real server-side API that pulls a system property's current value inside a script.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against treating every property change as automatically low-risk?
options: Property changes always require a full system outage
A property can affect every user or every record on the instance immediately on save, with no staging or approval gate
Properties are actually more dangerous to change than Business Rules in every case
Property values cannot be reverted once saved
questions.explain: Because editing a property needs no scripting or Update Set step beyond the record itself, it's easy to underestimate its instance-wide, immediate effect.
